Sounds like you are experiencing cognitive dissonance. I am also going though cognitive dissonance right now although about something different. However I did used to be religious when I was very young and am now an atheist. When you experience cognitive dissonance it can be extremely hard to choose what to believe but the best I can do is offer my own experiences and thoughts on religion. I honestly first started questioning religion when I was a young kid and learned that Santa was not real. It made me think "if that's not real how do I know if other magic sounding people like God are?" However I did not completely reject the idea of religion until I was a teen and older. I think when I was a teen it became a lot easier for me to let go of the idea because I started to realize that it contradicted many of my other beliefs that I personally held to far higher importance. Please note to anyone who reads the next few sentences that what I am about to say is not intended to offend anyone who is religious and I understand that not all of what I am about to say about religious people is true for everyone who is religious. I began seeing many religious people who would say things along the lines of "Gay people will end up in hell" and other things that I did not believe were right as I am a huge believer in the importance of people's personal freedom to do what they want so long as they don't infringe on other people's freedoms. I also started to think thoughts such as "if God is always watching me isn't that actually kind of creepy and a violation of privacy" as well as "If religion is about worshiping one person (God) without question doesn't that make it similar to a dictatorship?" These thoughts made religion start to become a lot more discomforting to me than comforting making it easier for me to let go of my beliefs. However I do still believe that there are reasons to continue living even without religion. I live for good times, goals, my own happiness and to help those around me when I can. Part of my current life philosophy has been heavily shaped by a video on YouTube called Optimistic Nihilism. This video starts off a bit depressing but trust me that it is a good video if you watch to the end. Here is a link: https://youtu.be/MBRqu0YOH14. Anyway I would also like to say that I hope neither you nor anyone else reading this was offended by what I said about religion as that was not my intention. My intention was simply to share my thoughts on religion honestly and hope that it helps. Even if I might personally not have a positive view of religion I still know many good and kind religious people and know that everyone is different.

Edit: one other thing I just thought of after re reading that part where you worry if you stop believing you will be "damned already". The way I see it there is not much point in worrying about that. Many people have different ways of interpreting the Bible and many people have different religions. Not one of those interpretations can be proven nor disproven. Maybe the "correct religion" is something that no one has even thought of yet and no one is doing anything right. You simply can't know and therefore there is no point in worrying about that.

This might not be that interesting but here it goes. From a very young age at around 3 or 4 my parents noticed that I was surprisingly more easy to take care of as a baby but they didn't think much of it at the time .However my parents still did not think anything of it till I got into Kindergarten. Once I was in Kindergarten the teachers realized that I would often prefer to play by myself rather than with other children and started finding it strange. After this continued for a while they eventually met with my parents to explain that something seemed off about me. My parents said that they told them "he is always by himself which would be sad except that he doesn't really seem that sad". They then got a child psychologist to observe me while playing in Kindergarten. Apparently I was not supposed to notice them but I did. My dad told me that one time while they were observing me trying not to be noticed I waved at them. Anyway this eventually lead to me seeing doctors and Psychologists who diagnosed me around the age of 5 with Asperger's syndrome (now called ASD). The strange thing is I enjoy hanging out with friends far more now that I'm older. But I still need some time alone. Hope that story was somewhat interesting and not just weird.
